card.title: Bond Characteristics — Length, Ionic Character and Dipole Moment

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: Bond parameters turn bonding into measurement. **Bond length** — the equilibrium internuclear distance, the sum of covalent radii — shrinks as bond order rises (C–C 154 → C≡C 120 pm) and grows as atoms enlarge (H–F 92 → H–I 160 pm), moving inversely with bond strength.…

rows.label: Formula
rows.text: - μ = q × d; 1 D = 3.33564 × 10⁻³⁰ C·m - % ionic character = μ(observed)/μ(100% ionic) × 100 - Hannay–Smyth: % ionic = 16(ΔEN) + 3.5(ΔEN)² - Covalent radius = ½ internuclear distance (homonuclear)

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Zero dipole ≠ nonpolar bonds:** CO₂'s bonds are highly polar; the *molecule* is nonpolar. State both facts when answering.  ·  **NF₃ vs NH₃:** same shape, opposite dipole logic — in NF₃ the bond dipoles oppose the lone pair's contribution (0.24 D); in NH₃ they reinforce it (1.47 D).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: "Dipole moment is the product of the magnitude of charge at one end and the distance between the opposite charges; it measures the polarity of a bond or molecule."

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: ***Cis/trans discrimination*** — cis-1,2-dichloroethene 1.90 D vs trans 0 D: identical formula, identical bonds, geometry alone separates them on the dipole meter.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: Verified PYQ context: NEB 2024 (bank 02) asked hydrogen bonding/water bp — its polarity foundation sits in this topic. The CO₂/SO₂ dipole contrast and HF calculation above are NEB-style practice; no standalone dipole-moment PYQ exists in the bank yet.

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: ## 1. Topic Introduction — Measuring the Unevenness of Bonds A bond between unlike atoms is rarely purely ionic or purely covalent — it sits somewhere between, and three measurable quantities locate its position: **bond length** (how close the nuclei sit), **ionic character** (how far charge has shifted), and **dipole moment** (the electrical signature of that shift).…  ·  ## 2. Fundamental Concepts ### 2.1 Bond length - **Definition:** the equilibrium internuclear distance between the centres of two bonded atoms. - Measured by X-ray/electron diffraction or spectroscopy; equals the **sum of covalent radii** of the two atoms (covalent radius = half the internuclear distance in a homonuclear bond).…

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: μ = 0 club: CO₂, BF₃, CH₄, CCl₄, PCl₅, SF₆, trans-isomers, para-isomers. Ionic % ladder: HF 43 > HCl 17 > HBr 11 > HI 5. Length ladder: C–C 154 > C=C 134 > C≡C 120.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: **NEB-style (3m): Explain why CO₂ has zero dipole moment while SO₂ has a significant one.** — **CO₂:** the molecule is linear (O=C=O, 180°). Each C=O bond is strongly polar, but the two bond dipoles are equal in magnitude and exactly opposite in direction along the same axis; their vector sum is zero, so μ(CO₂) = 0 D.…  ·  **NEB-style (3m): Calculate the percentage ionic character in HF (μ = 1.91 D, bond length = 92 pm).** — For a 100% ionic H–F bond the dipole would be one full electron charge separated by the bond length: μ(ionic) = q × d = (1.602 × 10⁻¹⁹ C) × (92 × 10⁻¹² m) = 1.47 × 10⁻²⁹ C·m. Converting: 1.47 × 10⁻²⁹ / 3.33564 × 10⁻³⁰ = **4.42 D**.…

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: For calculations, show the unit conversion: 1 D = 3.33564 × 10⁻³⁰ C·m, and quote μ(100% ionic) before dividing — the marker looks for q·d setup, not just the final 43%.

rows.label: Quick concepts
rows.text: Dipole moments were how chemists *measured* molecular shape before diffraction: zero moment → symmetric geometry (CO₂ linear, para-dichlorobenzene), nonzero → bent/pyramidal. One measurement, two topics of payoff.

rows.label: Key points
rows.text: Bond length: order↑ → length↓ (154/134/120 pm C–C family); size↑ → length↓ the reverse. Dipole moment μ = q·d, unit debye (1 D = 3.33564 × 10⁻³⁰ C·m), vector sum over all bonds. Symmetric molecules (CO₂, BF₃, CH₄, CCl₄, trans-isomers) → μ = 0 despite polar bonds.…

rows.label: Universal facts
rows.text: Water's 1.85 D moment is why microwave ovens work — the rotating dipole absorbs 2.45 GHz radiation; a symmetric molecule like CO₂ would be transparent.

Common Confusions **Polar bonds ≠ polar molecule:** CO₂ and CCl₄ have polar bonds but zero net moment — symmetry cancels. Polarity of a molecule is a vector question, not a bond question.  ·  **Dipole direction convention:** the chemists' arrow points from positive to negative (crossed tail at δ⁺); physics defines the vector the opposite way. Quote μ magnitudes, not directions, unless the convention is stated.

rows.label: More ideas
rows.text: **Ionic character is not all-or-nothing:** HF is 43% ionic and 57% covalent simultaneously — real bonds are mixtures, which is why Fajan's rules (topic 28) modulate ionic compounds toward covalency.  ·  ## 7.
